raw:
{
  "question_intent": "Bank earnings-call question about US Consumer Bank's Q2 clean run rate, Q1 level, sustainability of growth, and IB hedge allocation.",
  "main_topics": ["US Consumer Bank Q2 clean run rate", "Sustainability of growth into 2027, 2028", "IB hedge allocation"],
  "answer_completeness": "Complete",
  "response_stance": "Direct",
  "evidence_level": "High",
  "contains_numeric_evidence": true,
  "contains_forward_guidance": false,
  "narrative_alignment": "Aligned",
  "question_quote": "The first question is very much on that last point on the US Consumer [Bank]. I'm just trying to get to what the clean run rate was in Q2 and then how we get to that Q1 level. So, I think if you take out the American Airlines gain on sale, you account for an extra month of Best Egg and take out a bit of [American Airlines underlying income, you get to] the £900 [million] type Q2 income number, maybe fractionally below. I guess the positive takeaway from that, is if we do get back to that Q1 level within two three quarters, that's a real good pace of growth. Is that the right interpretation? How do we think about sustainability of that level of growth into 2027, into 2028? I mean I know that you talked about the securitised margins being a little compressed and maybe that's a bit lumpy, but it does imply a really strong pace of growth in this franchise and maybe you can talk about Samsung and pace of income contribution there? And the second question was just on the IB and the hedge, I guess it's something you probably don't think about that much in terms of structural hedge contributions in the Investment Bank, where does that allocate through in terms of the different lines? That'd be really helpful. I'd say it's not something we tend to think about with other UK banks for instance.",
  "answer_quote": "Okay. So let me start with the US Consumer [Bank], appreciate it is a very noisy quarter. The only thing I'd add to what you described is there was also a day one impairment impact of £26 million. So, I'd take account of that as well. The growth from here is going to come from a number of areas. Clearly, we are going to have organic growth from cards and you can see our businesses, the partners that we've got producing really well. I'd call out General Motors, which has had a really strong start. I'd expect to continue to see that margin growth as we grow deposits and continue to move towards a more retail focused business or a more balanced business. You are going to see growth from Samsung, but it is a de novo partnership. So, starting from zero. So, whilst it's strategically important, it's going to be quite small to start with. So, I wouldn't over rely on that. The other thing I would just call out is that, think of Best Egg in the same way as we described Tesco [Bank] to you, which was initially you're going to get funding synergies. Remember it has external banking relationships, both for its funding but also its securitisation and then that forward flow, all of that will get internalised. That will create some revenue related synergies into that business. You will see those before you see meaningful balance. So you're going to see this build gradually over time. And then on the IB hedge, just so everybody understands. Meaningfully, the hedge in the IB comes from the equity structural hedge, which is clearly smaller than the product structural hedge, but is important. The equity in the firm is growing. The way we allocate that to businesses is through RWA utilisation. So, you're going to see a higher level in areas where we have heavy RWAs, which is why you see quite a substantive part of that landing within the Investment Bank. And you should think that Markets would attract a bit more than that, more of that than Banking per se. There will be a small amount in the International Corporate Bank on the product structural hedge, but it's pretty modest given the sophistication of those clients, but coming through the NII line.",
  "reason": "The response directly addresses the question's intent, provides a complete answer with high evidence level, including numeric evidence, and aligns with the narrative of the question. The answer also includes forward guidance and discusses the sustainability of growth and IB hedge allocation."
}
